newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Unibanco still a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Unibanco still a buy.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said in a report it maintained its buy rating on Brazilian private bank Unibanco.

-- also said it revised its estimates previously in Brazilian reais to U.S. dollars to reflect the fact that the most liquid security of the bank will be the Global Depositary Shares (GDS) listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
-- Unibanco began trading on the NYSE in late May.

-- "Mostly as a consequence of this new currency expression, we have revised our earnings estimates for Unibanco to $4.25 in 1998 from 4.48 reais," analysts Jose A. Garcia-Cantera, Pablo Burbridge and Augusto Lange said in the report.

-- also said they maintained the same earnings estimate in U.S. dollars for 1997 "because the negative effects of the currency conversion should be compensated by better operating income than we previously expected due to the remuneration of reserve requirements on time deposits."

-- Salomon Brothers said improvement of efficiency levels at Unibanco should be a key driver of profitability in the coming years. It also said it estimates the bank will start reaping the rewards of the merger with Banco Nacional in 1997, when operating expenses will remain fairly flat.
-- Unibanco took over the healthy portion of Nacional in November 1995.
-- Unibanco preferred closed off 2.4 percent at 41.97 reais on the Sao Paulo bolsa.
-- Its ADR was up 1/8 at 40 in New York.
